newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian government sets deadline in wage talks.
newsitem.headline: Belgian government sets deadline in wage talks.

text.p: Belgian unions and employers talks on an agreeement on wages and jobs for the 1997-98 period must come to a conclusion by the end of November or the government will impose a deal, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's office said on Monday.
"They have until the end of the month to reach an agreement on a wage cap and jobs, but after that the government will take its responsibility," Dehaene's spokeswoman said.
She was speaking after union and employer representatives met with Dehaene on Monday one week after a 24-hour strike by a leading union brought negotiations to a standstill.
The wage and job talks are due to resume presently.

A government-imposed two-year wage freeze ends on December 31. Unions and employers can agree on nation-wide wage rises in the private sector for the next two years as long as Belgian wages do not rise more than those of Belgium's three main trading partners Germany, France and the Netherlands.
